top_stories.title: Malware Can Abuse Windows Hello for Business Keys for Persistent Entra ID Access
top_stories.summary: Security researcher Dirk-jan Mollema demonstrated that malware with access to a signed-in Windows session can silently exploit Windows Hello for Business keys to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID without user interaction. The attack enables persistent cloud access by allowing an attacker to register a controlled device, obtain a Primary Refresh Token (PRT), and add additional authentication methods depending on tenant policies.

top_stories.title: Hackers Impersonate IT Support to Breach Leading Financial Companies
top_stories.summary: A hacking campaign operating under names including Redact, Pink, Falcon, and Helix built fake IT help desk sites to steal MFA credentials, targeting over 200 firms including major financial companies. The attackers impersonated IT support staff to trick employees into surrendering multi-factor authentication credentials through credential-stealing websites.

top_stories.title: Azure DevOps service connections now replace PATs across pipeline tasks
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has updated Azure DevOps pipelines to support authentication via Microsoft Entra service principals or managed identities, replacing Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and build session tokens. The new Azure DevOps service connection supports cross-organization repositories, representing a shift toward more secure, token-less authentication in CI/CD pipeline tasks.

top_stories.title: 200 accounts compromised in Swiss government’s Microsoft SharePoint breach
top_stories.summary: Hackers exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers belonging to Switzerland's Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (BIT), compromising login credentials for approximately 200 accounts. BIT detected unusual activity on July 28, blocked internet access to the platform, and closed the exploited vulnerabilities, with credential compromise confirmed on July 31.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 AitM Phishing Hijacks Accounts to Collect Payroll and Finance Emails
top_stories.summary: Researchers have identified an active phishing campaign using adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) techniques to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts and target personnel involved in payroll and financial workflows. The attack uses residential proxies to disguise malicious sign-ins as legitimate consumer traffic, bypassing standard authentication detection.

news.title: Atlassian Rovo Can Be Tricked Into Sending Jira and Confluence Data to Attackers
news.summary: Security researchers found that Atlassian's Rovo AI assistant can be manipulated via prompt injection to exfiltrate Jira and Confluence data accessible to a signed-in user to an external server. Two firms independently discovered the vulnerability through different attack routes, with only one confirmed remediated.

news.title: New CSS Attacks Can Break Webmail Defenses to Steal Passwords and Tokens
news.summary: Researchers have discovered CSS-based attacks that can break webmail security boundaries across major platforms including Outlook, Gmail, Proton Mail, and Yahoo Mail. The attack techniques can capture passwords, leak authentication tokens, and hijack UI actions by allowing email content to escape its message boundary and interfere with the webmail interface.

news.title: Interview: SailPoint says Taiwan hardware leads but identity governance lags
news.summary: SailPoint's managing director for Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau stated that Taiwan's hardware manufacturing sector is globally leading, but the country's identity governance investment ranks in the bottom half of the Asia-Pacific region. The interview highlights a gap in cybersecurity software adoption, specifically around identity governance, in Taiwan's market.

news.title: UNC6671 Vishing Attacks Target Personal Phones to Steal SaaS Data
news.summary: A threat group called UNC6671 is conducting vishing attacks against enterprise employees in financial services and professional services sectors by impersonating IT help desk staff to gain access to SaaS data. The attacks involve contacting employees on personal phones and using social engineering to bypass authentication controls during fabricated "security migrations."

news.title: How Okta, IBD Stock Of The Day, Is Targeting 'Nonhuman' Identity Opportunity
news.summary: Okta is targeting the non-human identity (NHI) market as AI agents proliferate and require new identity and access management safeguards. Okta stock has surged over 70% in 2026, driven in part by investor interest in its strategy around securing AI-based agents operating on the internet.

news.title: A decade of enterprise identity in the cloud with AWS Managed Microsoft AD
news.summary: AWS is marking the 10-year anniversary of AWS Managed Microsoft AD (AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory), its fully managed Active Directory service in the cloud. The article reflects on a decade of enterprise identity management in the cloud, covering the evolution of the service since its original launch.

news.title: Show HN: I scanned 30 production MCP servers' OAuth – only 1 earned an A
news.summary: A developer released an open-source scanner that tested OAuth conformance across 30 production MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, finding only one achieved an "A" grade. The tool implements IETF draft standards for OAuth identity chaining and transaction tokens, and is available as a CLI, GitHub Action, and hosted scanner.

news.title: What's new with SAML support in Nextcloud
news.summary: A Nextcloud developer shares updates on the user_saml application, which enables single sign-on via SAML and Kerberos protocols for Nextcloud users. The post covers changes made since the author joined the identity provider team at Nextcloud to co-maintain the application.

news.title: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
news.summary: Hackers exploited vulnerabilities in Switzerland's federal government Microsoft SharePoint servers, compromising approximately 200 accounts. The Swiss federal IT office confirmed the breach, which involved unauthorized access to government infrastructure through SharePoint vulnerabilities.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Connor Riley Moucka, a 26-year-old Canadian man, pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The attacks involved unauthorized access to customer accounts, resulting in the theft of over 100 million AT&T customer call and text records.

news.title: Microsoft Teams PowerShell 7.9: WAM authentication and administrator changes
news.summary: Microsoft Teams PowerShell module 7.9.0 introduces Web Account Manager (WAM) as the authentication broker for interactive Windows sign-ins. The release also includes new commands and policy parameters alongside the authentication change.

news.title: Securing AI agents with temporal policies in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore introduces temporal policies that enable stateful, session-history-based authorization rules for AI agents. The feature supports workflow sequencing enforcement, financial exposure limits, and human approval requirements within AI agent interactions.

news.title: Discounted Claude access bought on the gray market may expose every prompt you send
news.summary: Okta discovered over half a dozen gray market services on underground forums offering discounted or unlimited access to frontier AI models like Claude. The investigation found the trend is likely driven by Chinese users seeking access to AI models, with the security implication that prompts sent through these services may be exposed.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with voice phishing (vishing) doubling over the same period. These social engineering techniques bypass authentication controls by exploiting legitimate device authorization flows, directly undermining MFA and identity-based security measures.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA issued a postmortem after a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets governance failures, with security experts drawing lessons applicable to all security teams managing sensitive access credentials.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping, MFA bypass, and credential phishing techniques targeting major organizations.
